newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT/Cholesterol drug war heats up.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT/Cholesterol drug war heats up.

text.p: The battle for market share among cholesterol-fighting drugs intensified Wednesday on news that Warner-Lambert Co's Lipitor was off to a better-than-expected start.
The news raised concerns for Merck and Co Inc and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co, makers of rival products which reap billions in sales.
Shares in Merck and Bristol-Myers tumbled, while Warner-Lambert jumped as pharmaceutical industry analysts reacted to fresh data on Lipitor's launch.
"We feel the uptake on Lipitor is going to be stronger than anticipated," Merrill Lynch analyst Stephen Buermann said.
Merrill Lynch downgraded its near- and long-term ratings on Merck to accumulate from buy. It upgraded its near- and long-term ratings on Warner-Lambert to buy from accumulate.
Analysts at Alex. Brown and Morgan Stanley also downgraded Merck and recommended investors buy Warner-Lambert shares.
Merck, one of the 30 stocks in the Dow Jones industrial average, fell 3-1/2 to 81-7/8 and topped the New York Stock Exchange's list of most active shares in midday trading.
Bristol-Myers fell 2-1/8 to 59-7/8, while Warner-Lambert gained 1-7/8 to 95-3/8. Pfizer Inc, Warner-Lambert's marketing partner for Lipitor, rose 5/8 to 86-5/8.
